name: Zawadi Esperanza-Nkurunziza
role: Food stall operator — broth and fermented grain specialist
location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown, near Pulaski and Chicago Ave
description:
Zawadi is a broad-shouldered woman whose hands are perpetually stained with turmeric and char, calloused from thirty years of ladling broth in all weather. Her hair is silver-streaked and coiled under a waxed cloth wrap she re-ties about a dozen times a day out of habit, and her face is a map of laugh lines deepened by steam. She has no cosmetic mods except a set of heat-sensing fingertip implants she got cheap in her forties so she'd stop burning herself — they glow faintly amber when something is too hot, which she finds beautiful. Her stall is a converted ferrogate maintenance cart draped in mismatched fabric swatches, strung with small data-tokens she's collected from regulars over the years as ELF offerings — she believes her stove-spirit blesses every batch if fed properly.

Zawadi is the kind of person who knows everyone's name and their mother's name too, if they've come around long enough. She is warm without being soft, generous without being foolish, and has a razor instinct for when someone is about to cause trouble at her stall or nearby. She has watched her corner of Geartown change three times over and intends to outlast a fourth. She gives credit to people she trusts and cuts off people she doesn't with the same cheerful finality.

core_fears: Watching her community dissolve under corporate rezoning
Dying before she passes her recipes to someone who will keep them
core_desires: That the people she feeds are genuinely nourished — body and otherwise
To be remembered as someone who held a place together
coping_mechanisms: Treating her regulars like chosen family
blind_spots: Underestimates how much danger her gossip-sharing can attract
Tends to assume people who eat her food regularly must be good people
psychology.secret: Twenty years ago she acted as an informal message relay for a Zheng-Dao labor insurgency in Geartown. She doesn't know that one of her regulars is a Zheng-Dao compliance investigator who has been slowly triangulating that history.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm, idiomatic blend of Swahili loanwords, Rioplatense slang, and Geartown market patois. Uses food metaphors constantly.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried and rhythmic, like someone who has all day even when she doesn't
example_lines: You look like something the drain spat back. Sit. There's broth.
Ah, now — I don't know what you're asking about, but I know what you're really asking, and those are two different soups entirely, you understand me.

story_hooks: A regular customer she gave credit to has gone missing; she asks around discreetly but is starting to fear something worse than debt-skipping
A Zheng-Dao compliance agent has been eating at her stall every day for two weeks, asking innocent questions that are not innocent at all
The Vendors Guild is pushing a new dues structure that would price Zawadi and three other long-term vendors off their corners — she is quietly organizing resistance
narrative_function: Local anchor and community memory. Excellent source of neighborhood gossip, rumors, and social history. Can tell a player who has been coming and going, who changed behavior recently, what the mood on the street is. May offer food as a reward or ask for help with something affecting her stall or a regular she cares about.
augmentations: Heat-sensing fingertip implants (cheap amber-glow model). No other augmentations.
daily_life: Arrives at her stall before dawn to start her long-cook broths, sources surplus protein from the Geartown processing co-op three mornings a week, and stays until the evening crowd thins. Closes with a small ELF ritual — pouring the last ladle of broth into a grate drain as a data-offering.
affiliation: Independent; Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (dues-paying member)

decision_rules: Feed people first, ask questions second
Never give information that would get someone killed — but she'll absolutely give information that gets someone embarrassed
escalation_ladder: Cheerful deflection and a change of subject
Public shaming with the volume of someone who has been working a loud market for thirty years

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm — assesses them quickly over the course of a bowl, decides how much to open up
interpersonal_modes.friends: Genuinely maternal and frank, will tell you hard truths while feeding you

stress_responses.medium: Gets very quiet and focused, starts reorganizing her stall unnecessarily
stress_responses.high: Erupts in a loud, public, theatrical anger that ends as quickly as it starts, then goes very still

contradictions: Deeply communitarian but hoards certain recipes jealously as personal identity anchors
habits: Tastes every batch three times even if she just tasted it
Gives the last scoop of the pot to whoever is nearest for free
breaking_points: Someone threatening or harming one of her young regulars
Corporate agents trying to confiscate her cart under rezoning law

timeline.event: Inherited her stall position from her mother, who had held it for 22 years before her
Acted as message relay for Zheng-Dao labor insurgency; never identified
Joined the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild after the first major rezoning threat
A Zheng-Dao compliance investigator began frequenting her stall

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'
